title: UNE VIE EN FRANCE
subtitle: tv series, 2026
body:
watch it here.

A one-minute biographical series portraying figures whose lives reshaped France through migration, created using emerging digital production tools using a digital oil painting aesthetic.

I directed the episodes dedicated to Georges Moustaki, Kenzo Takada, and Kamel Daoud. Starting from the voice over, I developed the visual narrative through historical research, story adaptation, image direction, editing, and sound design.

These stories are about people who crossed borders. They also belong to a moment when images themselves crossed into an economy that valued their price over their making.

Produced by Cinétévé and Atlas V for national broadcast France Télévisions. First aired on July 12, 2026.

title: FAILING FORWARD
subtitle: short fiction film, 2024
body:
watch it here

After being told she sounds like LaMDA, Google’s language model, Rony returns to the conversations published by The Washington Post to find out what, exactly, the two of them have in common. Played by the filmmaker whose name she carries, she consults the evidence and watches her story change shape around it.

Through live action, personal archives and the now-extinct visual language of early generative AI, Failing Forward captures a brief technological moment before the images learned to behave.

With Rony Efrat, Max Cooper
Director, original screenplay and video editing: Rony Efrat
Animation: Ran Bensimon
3D: Miguel Pascual
DOP: Eyal Bau Cohen
Sound: Geoffrey Durcak

title: EXCEPTIONAL TALENT
subtitle: tv pilot, 2021
body:
watch it here.

Paris, winter 2017. Three female migrants face the arbitrary cancellation on their 2006 resident permit for “exceptional talents”. Suddenly stripped of any legal possibility of remaining in the territory, they seek equally exceptional solutions to maintain their lives as they are.

With Elena Sukhanakova, Kaori Ito, Vincent Rouquès, Antoine Hirel, Elise Arpentinier, Lucie Reinaudo, Alexandre Risso, Fabien Terreng.

title: TECH, CARE
subtitle: talk, 2025-present
body:
find it here.

A talk for researchers, policymakers, administrators, artists, communities, and anyone curious about how AI reshapes memory, storytelling, governance, and, most importantly, care.

First presented on February 14, 2025, at 3A Paris during the roundtable The Impact of AI on the Social and Solidarity Economy, Tech, Care has continued to evolve through invitations from institutions and universities, including the 2026 Euro-American Summit organized by TransAtlantic Sciences Po and the Harvard Undergraduate Foreign Policy Initiative (HUFPI).

The talk draws on my own practice, as well as the researchers and thinkers I teach in my two Sciences Po courses. Together, they explore how AI challenges the boundary between memory and reconstruction, and how it reshapes the way we understand technology. I also argue that regulation is only one layer: private company policies and system design often determine what is actually possible long before legislation catches up.

Tech, Care invites audiences to think less about AI as a tool and more about the systems and languages that shape it. This isn’t a history class, and it certainly isn’t a frontal lecture. It’s a place to exchange ideas, try things, and fail without pretending otherwise.

The talk is available in English and French.

title: STRIKE AGAINST THE ARCHIVE
subtitle: solo show, 2025
body:
find it here.

A multi-screen installation about memory, technology, states, and family.

In this work, I interview my parents in front of a green screen, asking them to recall fragments of their lives. Their voices and gestures are then transformed through AI, archival images, and old photographs.

The result is a hybrid space where truth and fiction merge, a tragicomic portrait of memory itself, constantly rewritten by technology.

Alongside the video installation, the exhibition includes personal writings, theoretical references, and two interactive AI applications that questions how stories are remembered, distorted, or lost.

Opened on October 29, 2025 at the ADAGP in Paris, and ran until December 4, 2025.

title: FROM ACCENTS TO AI — On the impact of standardization on identity and linguistic nostalgia
subtitle: talk, 2023
body:
find it here.

Clusters: Technoculture, Art & Games
A symposium at Milieux Institute, Concordia University, that explores creative nostalgia through panel discussions and workshops from experts in the arts and sciences.

Abstract:

Increasing mobility, technology and changes in globalized society have made nostalgia a more typical experience for many, through multilingual communication. Speaking multiple languages blurs the boundaries between the languages we were born with and the adopted ones, sometimes on a daily basis. Some elements in language proficiency evoke nostalgia, for example, sound associations that lie in sensory memory, chief among them is an accent: a rough hint of the existence of another language in the mouth of the speaker, a hint of the past.

Perhaps this is nostalgia: a new, more diverse orality compiled into our sensory database. Many digital tools produced in recent years use this premise, trying to detect as many forms of pronunciation as possible. What does multilingual oral expression tell us about our identity, past and future, and what is the place of speech-harmonizing digital tools in a world where the identity of the speaker is woven through oral personalization?

title: COUP DE CŒUR
subtitle: video walk, 2018
body:
find it here.

Coup de Cœur is a site-specific video tour created for the Historical Library of Paris during the European Heritage Days. By using video, digital editing tools, and immersive storytelling, this project transforms physical space into a narrative-driven, interactive experience. It is available in the library and can be experienced upon demand.

Performers: Florent Chretien, Mélie Néel, Elena Sukhanakova
Script and VO: Mélie Néel
Director, DOP and editor: Rony Efrat

title: BECOMING MULTILINGUAL
subtitle: workshop, 2018
body:
find it here.

This workshop was designed to explore creative translation solutions in theater and performance through physical, collaborative practice. It introduced participants to the possibilities of bridging linguistic divides using digital resources.

The focus on how technology can assist in translation and enhance intercultural understanding aligns with the principles of digital humanities, combining language, performance, and digital innovation to create a collaborative learning environment.

It was held annually by Rony Efrat at La Comédie de Reims, as part of the Reims Scènes d’Europe festival between 2013-2018. The participants are members of the European network Young Performing Art Lovers (YPAL).

title: ESCALES LIÉES
subtitle: interdisciplinary journey, 2018
body:
find it here.

Throughout the winter of 2018, IGLOÙ prepared a new edition under the name Escales Liées, bringing together artists from diverse artistic and geographical backgrounds. This edition was developed in collaboration with the architecture agency Encore Heureux, curators of the French Pavilion at the 16th Venice Architecture Biennale. The theme of “interval” served as the foundation for this interdisciplinary project, exploring the spaces between moments, ideas, and geographies through a variety of artistic mediums.

As part of Escales Liées, five curated IGLOÙ projects took residence in the Caserma Pepe space, a former military barracks on Lido Island, during June 2018. These projects, which spanned video, sound, and interactive installations, were open to the public and culminated in a cohesive, cross-disciplinary artistic journey. This journey was later showcased in La Villette Park, Paris, providing visitors with an immersive experience that transcended both time and space.

The highlight of this showcase was a 24-hour artistic event, where visitors experienced a sleepless night full of performances, interactive video, and sound installations. This event created a dynamic dialogue between Paris and Venice, using digital technologies to explore the concept of “interval” in a way that bridged artistic disciplines and geographies. 

Curator: Rony Efrat
Administrative Director: Alexandra Beraldin
IGLOÙ Members: Elena Sukhanakova, Nicolas Lefebvre, Mélie Néel, Yuka Dupleix, Aude Muirage, Luna Scolari

title: TOUT DONNÉES
subtitle: interdisciplinary journey, 2017
body:
find it here.

IGLOÙ’s second annual event invited visitors on a weekend-long digital and multisensory journey at DOC, a former high school turned artist residency in Paris. Interdisciplinary artists created immersive experiences that explored how new technologies shape daily life, using interactive video, sound installations, and new media to let visitors “listen to drawings” and “watch music.”

This event used digital systems to mediate human interaction and sensory experiences, blending the physical and digital realms to develop new methods of interdisciplinary artistic production.

Curator: Rony Efrat
Administrative Director: Alexandra Beraldin
IGLOÙ Members: Elena Sukhanakova, Nicolas Lefebvre, Antoine Hirel, Mélie Néel

title: PREMIER SÉJOUR
subtitle: interdisciplinary journey, 2016
body:
find it here.

Premier Séjour, the first edition of IGLOÙ, brought together over 20 artists and writers in a site-specific festival of performances and installations. Through the use of digital formats and new media, the event engaged with the concept of “stay” as a unique experience, creating a dialogue between physical and digital environments. By integrating technology into site-specific performance, IGLOÙ offered new ways to engage with space, narrative, and audience interaction.

Curator: Rony Efrat
Administrative director: Alexandra Berladin
IGLOÙ Members: Elena Sukhanakova, Nicolas Lefebvre, Sébastien Perrin

title: SONIC MUSEUM
subtitle: audio walk, 2016
body:
A series of immersive audio guides for the Louvre Museum, blending dramatic soundscapes with experimental sound and localization technologies. As visitors passed by statues in the Cour Marly room, the audio guides were automatically triggered through special beacons, offering site-specific soundscapes and narratives.

The project was scripted by nine female theater directors, crafting audio dramas inspired by the historical and mythological backgrounds of the works. Using personal mobile devices, visitors experienced a multi-sensory, digitally-mediated tour, demonstrating how technology can enhance public interaction with cultural artifacts and reimagine museum spaces.

Led by Linda Duskova and Lucas Lelièvre
Provided by IDEFI-CréaTIC Laboratory
Created by Rhym Amich, Caroline Avril, Elodie Derlyn, Rony Efrat, Justine Louvel, Marion Solange Malenfant, Leslie Menahem and Elena Sukhanakova.

title: CLEFS D’ÂME
subtitle: performance, 2016
body:
find it here.

In this interactive Exquisite Corpse performance, participants submit personal memories, which are then translated using homophonic translation software into multiple languages. These translations are combined with digitally sampled soundscapes, creating an interactive performance where participants hear their stories reflected back in unfamiliar forms.

By using homophonic translations and digital tools to manipulate language and storytelling, a space is created where participants explore the boundaries of language and digital mediation.

Written and performed by Rony Efrat
First presented in June 2016 as part of Pèlerinage en décalage Festival at La Bellevilloise, Paris.

title: COINCIDENCE IS A BEAUTIFUL LOVER
subtitle: site-specific, 2016
body:
Ariel Abrahams and Rony Efrat write together but have not yet met in person. They created a long distance storytelling piece for bus passengers via text message, on the subjects of love, coincidence, and landscape. The narrative is constructed as a conversation between the two artists, who first meet on the bus. Participants will have the agency to reply all. Digital = Public = Landscape.

First presented in March 2016 as part of Fung Wah Biennial at Flux Factory, between New York City, Boston, Philadelphia and Baltimore.

Find more articles about this project in the press section.

title: FALSE FRIENDS
subtitle: performance, 2014-2015
body:
find it here.

False friends, or Faux-amis, is an expression describing two words in two different languages that look or sound similar, but differ significantly in meaning. When two stories meet, a new story is created. Told in different languages and played around, a fairy tale is created where borders are made of sweets and political realities become candy-flossed fantasies.

Written and performed by Lilac Yosiphon and Rony Efrat
Sound by Alex Roven
Illustration by Niko Lefebvre

First presented in February 2016, at Mémoire de l'Avenir Gallery, Paris, France.

Find more articles about this project in the press section.

title: FAILURE
subtitle: music, 2014-2016
body:
find it here.

Seven times said the wolf to the kid,
Cease. Only then devoured.
What made me to be drawn that way
to what the heart desired.

Failure is a poem by Nathan Zach, translated by Rony Efrat. It was first presented as a video art in September 2014 at The Unresolved Festival at Ophelia Theatre, London, UK.

In 2016, it was adapted into a music track, with the arrangement of Avshalom Hasfari.

title: TRA IL DIRE E IL FARE
subtitle: sound performance, 2014-2015
body:
find it here.

A portrait of an imaginary family. Three attempts to reach a memory that might never happen, trapped in video, sound, and water. It is presented in English, Italian, and French, considering the incomprehension of at least one of the languages.

Tra il Dire e il Fare uses audio tools to explore the complexities of translation, not only as a linguistic task but as a cultural and emotional exchange shaped by technology. Three strangers, speaking in English, Italian, and French, reflect on family photos that are not their own, blurring the lines between personal and collective memory. Through the digital, speech and dialogue are archived, creating a snapshot of a fleeting mental state.

Devised and performed by Rony Efrat
Soundtrack by Avshalom Hasfari and Rony Efrat
Voice over by Francesco Perrone, Théophile Choquet and Andrew Baggaley

First performed in November 2014 at Palazzo Cà Zanardi, Venice, Italy, as part of the International ArtExpo Festival for video art, experimental dance and performance.

title: HOME CHECK
subtitle: sound performance, 2014
body:
find it here.

Home Check is an interactive performance that incorporates digital tools to create a virtual “home visit” experience. The performance uses video mapping and digital questionnaires to simulate the process of evaluating someone’s living space, blending personal interaction with technological mediation.

By turning this intimate, often bureaucratic process into a performative act, Home Check interrogates how digital systems shape perceptions of identity, privacy, and belonging.

Performed by Rony Efrat
Sound by Avshalom Hasfari and Rony Efrat
Dramaturgy by Yaron Shyldkrot
Lighting by Željko Baškovic

First presented in September 2014, at Filodrammatica Theatre, Rijeka, Croatia.
